newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London lower on profit-taking.

text.p: U.S. shares were mostly lower in Europe on Friday as investors took profits following the Dow's near 170-point surge over the past two sessions.

Trading volumes were light as investors awaited a batch of U.S. economic data as well as next week's FOMC meeting, dealers said. "It's hardly surprising that people are locking in a bit of profit," one senior dealer said.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see profit-taking in New York today ahead of the weekend. This week has been hectic and there won't be any let up next week."
The near-term focus will be on U.S. Q4 GDP data for December, due at 1330 GMT. Also of interest will be the U.S. Chicago Purchasing Managers and New Home sales for January.

Next week's data including U.S personal income, construction spending and the latest survey from the National Association of Purchasing Managers on Monday followed by leading indicators and factory orders due on Tuesday and Wednesday respectively.
The February 4 and 5 Fed monetary gathering will also be watched for the Fed's view on interest rate policy ahead of the the key U.S. non-farm payroll number for January.
David Coleman, economist at the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, does not expect a Fed rate rise next week but said a 25 basis point rise in March was possible.
"There is a case to be made for an insurance policy on rates," Coleman said.

The Fed took out such an insurance policy on February 4, 1994, when it bumped up its funds rate by 25 basis points to try to prevent a spike in U.S. inflation and Coleman said history could repeat itself in March if upcoming data point to a stronger U.S. economy.
High-technology shares led the general decline. IBM was down $1/2 at $157-3/8, Intel slipped $3/4 to $159-3/8 and Texas Instruments fell $1/4 to $74-3/8.
